reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: The LOG_FAILED AtomicBool owns a sticky log-output failure bit initialized false; it owns neither logfile nor namelogfile.
owner_creation.invariant: The failure latch contains no resource pointer.

aliases_escapes.analysis: logfile_failed copies LOG_FAILED; swap changes no input-buffer reference and exposes no address to a caller.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Observers receive values rather than mutable aliases.

callback_targets.analysis: The first transition calls io_error_diagnostic directly with a static byte string; the LOG_FAILED flag cannot store a logging callback.
callback_targets.invariant: Failure reporting does not retain a callback context.

invalidation.analysis: The LOG_FAILED bit is never reset in maintained code, so later buffer/file replacement cannot invalidate the previously recorded failure.
invalidation.invariant: A logged failure remains sticky until process exit.

mutation_commit.analysis: swap(true) precedes the diagnostic; Relaxed is sufficient because the LOG_FAILED latch does not publish any accompanying owned payload.
mutation_commit.invariant: The first reporter records failure before emitting output.

release_pair.analysis: LOG_FAILED owns no FD or filename; write_log_buffer/end_logfile separately close logfile and free namelogfile.
release_pair.invariant: Resource cleanup is separate from the failure bit.

error_cleanup.analysis: A failed best-effort diagnostic leaves LOG_FAILED set and acquires no new diagnostic allocation requiring cleanup.
error_cleanup.invariant: Reporting failure cannot reset the recorded log error.

signals_handoff.analysis: Atomic accesses protect this LOG_FAILED bit only; they do not make input lists, log descriptor teardown or asynchronous quit safe.
signals_handoff.invariant: Latch review does not approve surrounding handler reentry.
limitations: Only this failure latch is clear; M0-IO-004 and raw file/log ownership remain separate open obligations.

finding_context.M0-IO-004: Context only: this entry reviews storage ownership, not the caller/application mechanism in M0-IO-004. That finding stays open and this clear storage disposition does not resolve or approve it.
